label: early original-phase input f (t<=3) or q/j/g (t=1-2)
explanation: Fires during the original input phase on a small set of input tokens at early positions: f at any of positions 0-3, and q, j, g at positions 1-2. Positions 1-2 carry about 78% of the activation mass. f is the strongest trigger, with the largest activations (up to max) on f at t=1, often after a first token i. q/j/g fire more weakly, around 0.2-0.4 of max. A repeat f later in the early window gives weaker activations. Does not fire on the delimiter, does not fire in the copy phase (only 180 tiny activations there), and does not fire at t>=4. It does not fire on any other letter or digit, apart from tiny activations (<0.05 of max) on z at t=1 and rare ones on c. Dev split: precision 1.0, recall 0.98, mass recall 0.999.

issues: The core claims hold. Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.979, mass recall 0.998. There are 0 false positives, and every missed activation sits in the lowest activation quartile (quartile coverage 0.917 / 1 / 1 / 1).

The misses are small, low-mass activations: z at t=1 (about 0.02-0.03 of max), rare c, and tiny copy-phase activations such as 0.02 on f. Together they hold 0.2% of the mass. The explanation already mentions these, so they do not form an unexplained systematic class.
q/j/g at t=0 or t=3 never fire (score precision 0.0, recall 0.0). This confirms that the narrower position window for q/j/g is correct.
Copy phase: phase==2 has recall 0.001 and mass 0.0002, which matches the claim of only about 180 tiny activations. The delimiter has 0 activations.
Minor overstatement: 'does not fire at t>=4' is not strictly true. There are 37 activations at orig_idx 4 and about 180 copy-phase activations at later steps, all negligible.

Minor overstatement: 'often after a first token i' is weak. f at t=1 with orig(0)==i covers only 0.33% of actives (0.8% of mass), so 'often' is not supported by frequency, though precision is 1.0. Repeat f (n_seen f>0) is real but small (1.8% of actives, 2.6% of mass).
